subject: Activation ramp & edge fallback vetting for HelixHealth Dedicated Pool
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@helixhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation ramp for Dedicated Pool - initial ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We scoped a pilot traffic pattern against the Dedicated pool and a couple of questions came up from our infra team before we lock the go-live window: 

- Can Redwood guarantee per-request regional routing to our US-West region (we need sticky routing for data locality)?
- What are the burst policy limits and how are they billed during a 2–4 hour predictable spike?
- We have an edge fallback plan where, in case of pool saturation, requests route to a cached-host model in our VPC — any recommended throttling settings or token limits to avoid cold-starts?

I've attached our draft activation matrix (activation_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a rough network diagram of the fallback flow.

Goal: align on a final ramp timeline and the mutual action plan (MAP) this week so procurement can finish the paperwork.

Cheers,
Aaron
Aaron Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixHealth
Onsite: Palo Alto
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@helixhealth.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2029 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Activation ramp for Dedicated Pool - initial ask

Hi Aaron — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below, and I copied Monica (CS lead) to capture the implementation tasks: 

- Regional routing: yes — we can pin traffic to the US-West cluster. We’ll provide a routing policy that pins by customer and AZ preference. We’ll include a preflight checklist with the IP ranges and egress policies you need to whitelist.
- Burst policy: default burst tier covers short surges up to 3x baseline per-pool for 30 minutes; for predictable multi-hour spikes we recommend a scheduled burst window (reserved burst) which we can guarantee and invoice separately as committed burst hours. Monica, I’ll need the suggested thresholds for Helix’s traffic pattern.
- Edge fallback: recommended settings are 80% token throttling and a 5s client-side retry with linear backoff. We’ve seen that reduces cold-starts and keeps tail latency bounded.

Proposed MAP items this week:
1) Finalize activation matrix + schedule (Aaron + Priya + Monica)
2) Network/IP allowlist + telemetry hooks (NetOps)
3) Confirm reserved-burst hours and pricing (Sales Ops)
4) Dry-run on a low-traffic slice (Implementation + CS)

Can you confirm which date windows next week work for the dry-run? We can aim for Wed or Thu.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya@helixhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Dec 2029 16:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Activation ramp for Dedicated Pool - initial ask

Tessa, Aaron —

Wed works better for us. Proposed window: Dec 11, 09:00–12:00 PT for the dry-run (low traffic slice). For burst sizing: our ops observed ~2.8x baseline sustained for ~90 minutes during last month’s batch-job period — so a scheduled burst of 3x for 2 hours should cover the realistic case.

I'll attach a short doc with expected traffic curves and authorization contacts (will send after sync).

— Priya
Priya Rao
SRE Manager, HelixHealth
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@helixhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Dec 2029 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Activation ramp for Dedicated Pool - implementation notes and asklist

Thanks team — a few implementation specifics from Redwood's side: 

1) Autoscale & reserved burst config:
   - We'll create a dedicated pool with min_replicas: 4, max_replicas: 40 for US-West.
   - Reserved burst: add a scheduled policy (start/end + committed_burst_hours). Billing will be via the Dedicated reserved-burst SKU and applied to the next invoice.

2) Routing and stickiness:
   - We need a final list of HelixHealth CIDRs and preferred AZ failover order. 
   - Session affinity will be enforced via our routing token; please confirm any IPs that must bypass affinity.

3) KV prefix caching and TTLs for edge fallback:
   - Recommend cache TTL 30m for prediction results and a prefix key policy keyed by customer_id + model_variant.
   - If you prefer a longer TTL for the VPC-cached model, we can set adaptive invalidation based on anomaly signals.

4) Telemetry and acceptance criteria for the dry-run:
   - 95th p50/p95 token latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for the Dedicated pool.
   - Error rate < 0.5% during the scheduled burst window.

Action items (owners):
- Aaron / Priya: confirm CIDRs, AZ order, and the dry-run traffic slice (Due: 2029-12-06)
- Priyom Das (Implementation): assemble the cutover playbook and runbook artifacts (Due: 2029-12-09)
- Monica (CS): finalize reserved-burst proposal and pricing appendix (Due: 2029-12-07)

Attachments included: activation_matrix_v1.xlsx, edge_fallback_network_diagram.pdf

I'll create a shared folder and post the cutover playbook once Priyom drops the first draft.

— Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@helixhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@helixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Dec 2029 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Activation ramp for Dedicated Pool - cutover playbook initial draft

Attached is the initial cutover playbook outline (uploaded to the shared Drive link). High-level notes: 

- Preflight checklist (NetOps): firewall rules, egress ranges, DNS entries — validation script included.
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic for 30 minutes, validate logs and telemetry, then step to 25% / 60% before full cut.
- Escalation matrix: SRE on-call -> Redwood implementation on-call -> CS -> Escalation to Sales Ops for billing disputes.

Questions for Helix:
- Confirm SLA exception window acceptance for the 3x reserved burst period (billing and SLO forgiveness).
- Any internal compliance reviews needed for cross-AZ routing?

I'll iterate the playbook and upload v1.1 by EOD Friday. If everyone agrees to the draft, I'll schedule the kickoff runbook walk-through for Dec 9.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
